01 / The project

A recognizable world
for iMinerals.

A visual identity that gives a supplement range a warm, confident presence. Burgundy packaging, expressive type, and tactile imagery connect individual products to a wider brand experience.

The central design challenge: make the range feel clear, connected, and considered.

01

The problem

A supplement pack carries several layers of information. The brand, product name, formula descriptor, and quantity all need a place without competing for the same attention.

02

The opportunity

Create a recognizable identity that feels approachable in an everyday setting. Let people distinguish the product while still recognizing the family it belongs to.

03

The solution

A burgundy-led visual system, a prominent vertical brand name, and a clear information hierarchy. Natural light and tactile surfaces extend that character into the product imagery and digital design.

This case-study narrative is based on the supplied design work. The problem, audience, and rationale are proposed portfolio framing for review against the original project brief.

03 / The central idea

A daily ritual.
A considered identity.

Give the products a shared visual presence, then let the details do their individual jobs. The identity combines character at brand level with clarity at product level.

01 / Recognizable

A consistent signature.

Burgundy and the vertical wordmark act as repeatable cues across the product family.

02 / Readable

A clear reading order.

Contrasting type styles and sizes distinguish the brand, product identity, and supporting details.

03 / Approachable

A warmer setting.

Natural light, gentle shadows, and tactile materials connect the visual system to familiar surroundings.

04 / Colour direction

Warmth.
Contrast. Clarity.

The working palette comes from the artwork: deep burgundy, warm ivory, brushed silver, and dark ink. Each colour has a different role, from recognition to readability.

01

Anchor the identity.

Burgundy links the jars, product cards, and digital accents. Its depth gives the pale lettering a strong visual contrast.

02

Give the product space.

Ivory supports the warm lighting and quiet backgrounds, allowing the darker packaging to remain the focal point.

03

Introduce a material contrast.

Silver reflects the lid treatment and creates a cooler highlight against the warm glass and surfaces.

04

Keep information direct.

Dark ink provides a practical reading colour on light surfaces without introducing another competing accent.

These are presentation colours based on the artwork, not verified production or print specifications. The surrounding case-study page follows the portfolio’s lavender, charcoal, and off-white palette.

05 / Typography

Character for the brand.
Clarity for the details.

The packaging combines a tall, expressive serif wordmark with a direct sans serif for product information. The difference in form gives each layer a distinct job.

Expressive forms / Editorial character / Vertical signature

01 / Brand name

Build recognition through character.

The serif treatment has a distinctive silhouette. On the pack, its vertical placement creates an anchor at the left of the information area.

02 / Product name

ZINC
COMPLEX

A bold sans serif makes the product identity direct and easy to locate. Its simpler shapes give the detailed wordmark room to remain expressive.

03 / Supporting details

Product descriptor / Quantity

Smaller text, contained descriptors, and consistent alignment organize secondary information without giving every line equal emphasis.

The original font files have not been supplied. Georgia and Arial are illustrative specimens here; they demonstrate the serif/sans relationship without claiming to identify the original brand typefaces.

06 / Packaging hierarchy

One system.
Distinct products.

The pack gives the brand, product identity, and supporting details separate positions. A repeated structure allows individual formulas to sit within the same recognizable family.

Explore the reading order

A vertical signature.

The brand name runs along the left side of the label. Its orientation creates a recognizable edge and keeps the main product information in its own reading area.

The highlight is a case-study annotation. The underlying artwork is shown as supplied.

Keep the family recognizable.

The shared burgundy container, silver lid, and wordmark treatment create continuity between Zinc Complex and Probiotics.

Give the product priority.

The product name has its own scale and position. Supporting descriptors sit beneath it rather than competing with the brand signature.

Use spacing as structure.

Clear separation between the title, descriptor, and quantity makes the different information levels visible.

07 / Art direction

Natural light.
Product first.

Warm daylight, ceramics, and gentle shadows give the packaging a tactile setting. The surrounding objects support the product without competing with its colour or label.

The human perspective

From a product
to a daily ritual.

The hand-held capsule image introduces scale and a familiar action. It gives the brand story a human moment alongside the more composed product scenes.

Across the images, warm tones and restrained backgrounds maintain a shared atmosphere.

08 / Material & detail

The detail
builds the feel.

The product visualization brings the material treatment close: translucent burgundy, a brushed silver lid, pale lettering, and directional light.

01 / Depth

Let the glass carry colour.

The translucent burgundy creates variation through highlights and shadows. The colour becomes part of the object rather than a flat background alone.

02 / Contrast

Separate lid and jar.

The cooler silver treatment balances the warm container and makes the packaging silhouette easier to read.

03 / Restraint

Give small details space.

Close framing and a quiet setting put attention on the lettering, reflections, and material transitions.

Material descriptions refer to the visual treatment shown. Manufacturing materials and finishes have not been independently confirmed.

09 / Supporting digital design

The same identity,
online.

The website artwork carries the palette and product imagery into a broader brand story. Burgundy headings, generous white space, and nature-inspired scenes keep the digital presentation connected to the packaging.

01 / First impression

Lead with one focal point.

The hero places the product at the centre of the composition. Large burgundy type establishes a clear visual hierarchy above it.

02 / Exploration

Move from story to range.

Product cards provide a repeatable structure for browsing. Editorial and lifestyle sections then expand the visual world around the products.

03 / Continuity

Repeat the right cues.

Burgundy, rounded containers, and the same product treatment connect the page sections back to the identity.

This is the supplied website design artwork, not a functioning supplement shop.

10 / Design logic

From a visual idea
to a consistent system.

The project can be understood through four connected design decisions. This explains the relationship between the visible outputs without assuming a research or production process that has not been documented.

01 / Define

Set the visual character.

Establish warmth, contrast, and clarity as a shared direction for the identity and product presentation.

02 / Organize

Give information a place.

Separate the brand, product name, and supporting details through scale, alignment, and spacing.

03 / Connect

Build the family.

Repeat the colour, container treatment, and label logic while changing the product information.

04 / Extend

Carry the identity outward.

Apply the same visual cues to product cards, lifestyle imagery, material studies, and the digital experience.

11 / Design outcome

From a single pack
to a connected brand.

The palette, typography, packaging hierarchy, and image direction work together across the project. The outcome is a coherent visual presentation for iMinerals across brand, product, and digital touchpoints.

A recognizable identity.

Burgundy and the expressive brand name establish a consistent signature across the work.

A structured product family.

Shared packaging cues connect the range while giving each product a clear place in the system.

A wider visual world.

Product imagery, human moments, material detail, and website design extend the identity beyond the label.

This is a design outcome. No sales, conversion, customer-research, or commercial-launch results have been supplied.
